source_text.body:
Support ADHD executive function and job hunting with agents
A toolkit that helps people, especially those with ADHD, start using agents to support executive function, with modules for job search and tracking contacts.
·
Nov 14, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The kit is a set of instructions you paste into Claude Code or Codex (or a chat app) to turn it into an agent called XO. You start with a small real task, such as turning a scattered to-do list into one next action. XO saves notes as plain files only after you approve them. Optional modules include Kettle, an address book for finding contacts, and Advokat, an experimental job-search framework.
How it went
The source reports no results. It says the kit is new and not fully tested, and that the job-search module is experimental. It says the agent won't apply to jobs for you.
Worth knowing
Usage limits can run out mid-setup, since the apps have five-hour windows. Check your existing plan before paying, and expect to correct the AI's mistakes.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I have ADHD and struggle with starting tasks and keeping track of things. Help me set up a job search routine: ask me about [target roles, location, and weekly time available], then build a simple tracker for applications and contacts with columns for [company, role, status, next step, follow-up date]. Finish by giving me a tiny first-step checklist for this week and a short daily check-in routine I can follow.
Original source: https://proptermalone.github.io/xo-kit/index.html
